extracted.intended_audience: Applicants seeking admission to the USPTO registration examination (patent bar) to become patent agents/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying for admission to the USPTO registration examination (patent bar), demonstrating requisite scientific/technical training, application documentation, testing procedures, eligibility/ineligibility rules, and post-passage requirements. Covers Categories A–D, application form instructions, Prometric test administration, fees, refunds, and related procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possess necessary legal, scientific, and technical qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual will not be registered to practice before the USPTO unless that individual possesses the legal, scientific, and technical qualifications necessary to render applicants valuable service. Applicant bears the burden of showing the requisite scientific and technical training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching standard (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D); 37 CFR § 11.7). The Bulletin interprets how applicants typically demonstrate technical competence and explains review by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition pathways (Categories A–C and D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three categories, Categories A–C, may be used to demonstrate possession of required scientific and technical training to practice in all patent matters; Category D may enable practice in design patent matters only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not qualify under Categories A–D, the USPTO will conduct an independent review for compliance with § 11.7(a)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A: Degree in a recognized technical subject
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant has established necessary training if they provide an official transcript showing a bachelor's, master’s, or Ph.D. awarded in one of the listed subjects (extensive list including biology, chemistry, engineering, computer science*, physics, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acceptable computer science degree must be a bachelor of science degree from an accredited college or university. Official transcript is required (not diploma or copy); transcript must include university stamp or seal. The Office will accept degrees where the transcript demonstrates equivalence to a Category A degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Degree in another subject — equivalence through coursework
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a degree in a subject other than those listed in Category A must demonstrate scientific/technical training equivalent to a Category A degree by satisfying one of Options 1–4, other training, or other education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: (i) 24 semester hours in physics (physics-major courses only); (ii) 32 semester hours combination: 8 semester hours chemistry/physics (≥1 lab) + 24 semester hours in biology/botany/microbiology/molecular biology (science/engineering-major courses only); (iii) 30 semester hours in chemistry (chemistry-major courses only); (iv) 40 semester hours combination: 8 semester hours chemistry/physics/biology (≥1 lab) + 32 semester hours of chemistry/physics/biology/botany/microbiology/molecular biology/engineering. Transcripts and concurrent course descriptions required; only courses with grade of C- or better accepted; quarter/trimester conversion (multiply by 2/3); certified English translations required for foreign documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Transcripts and course descriptions requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Official transcripts are required to establish degree award and completion of each course relied upon; course descriptions concurrent with the year the course was taken must accompany the transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course descriptions must include: catalog cover page showing year, page(s) describing requirements for the major, and complete pages describing the courses. Applicant may send official transcript to OED directly or include official transcript issued to the applicant provided it includes university stamp or seal. Highlight courses to be considered to speed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Grades and course acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Only courses with a grade of C- or better will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To speed review, highlight the courses on transcripts and course descriptions. Only courses for science or engineering majors (as specified in options) will be accepted for certain options; e.g., physics courses must be for physics majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Quarter/trimester to semester conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert trimester credit hours or quarter hours into semester hours, multiply the quarter hours or trimester credit hours by 2/3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion needed when term lengths differ; semester hour defined as one hour of class instruction per week for one semester (typically 15–18 weeks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Other acceptable course work (computer science and design engineering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Option 4, up to four semester hours accepted for design engineering or drafting; computer science courses that stress theoretical foundations, analysis, and design and include substantial laboratory work (including software development) will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable CS courses include algorithms/data structures, software design with lab, programming languages with lab, computer organization/architecture, AI/robotics, networking, linear/logic circuits, operating systems, software methodology/engineering. Such courses may not substitute for the 8 semester hours of chemistry or physics required under Option 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Typical non-acceptable coursework
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses typifying what is not accepted: anthropology; astronomy; audited courses; behavioral science (psychology, sociology); continuing legal education; public health; technology policy; corporate-taught courses; management/business administration; software-use courses; data management/MIS; manual processing/fabrication skills; pass/fail courses; correspondence courses; field identification; high school level courses; mathematics courses; one-day conferences; patent law courses; paleontology; political science; repair/maintenance courses; radio operator license; science courses for non-science majors; vocational training; work study programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also excluded: college research or seminar courses without set content in course descriptions; courses that repeat or are lesser-included courses for which credit has already been given; courses that do not provide scientific and technical training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Other training and education equivalence (case-by-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other factors (foreign education, academic credit for work experience, military education, life experience, etc.) may be acceptable to the extent objective evidence demonstrates equivalence to accredited U.S. education in a Category A subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable evidence: specific courses accepted for college credit by an accredited U.S. college in a Category A subject; CLEP credit accepted by an accredited college; life experience credit identified in the college catalog as credit in a Category A subject; home study credit granted by institution accredited by Distance Education and Training Council; foreign education evaluated by private credential evaluators; credits from USDA Graduate School if accepted by accredited institutions. Applicant has burden of showing equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B — Military training/credit
rubrics_metrics.description: OED will not evaluate and award credit for military service per se, but credit may be granted for technical courses taken pursuant to military training if applicant shows semester-hour credit that would be credited toward a degree at an accredited U.S. college/university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should consult The ACE Military Guide and provide evidence of how courses would be credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category C: Practical engineering or scientific experience (FE test)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant relying on practical engineering or scientific experience may qualify by taking and passing the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) test. Official FE results and an official transcript showing award of a bachelor's degree must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FE test is developed and administered by State Boards of Engineering Examiners; contact appropriate State Boards for FE administration. The USPTO does not administer the FE test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D: Design patent practice only — degree in recognized design subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant qualifies for design patent practice only if they provide official transcript showing bachelor's, master’s, or Ph.D. awarded in subjects such as Architecture, Applied Arts, Fine/Studio Arts, Graphic Design, Art Teacher Education, Industrial Design, Product Design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants registered under Category D will be able to practice in design patent matters only. Official transcript requirements mirror Category A (official transcript with stamp/seal; equivalence may be accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Former USPTO employees — request for waiver under 37 CFR § 11.7(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Former Office employees (including patent examiners) seeking registration by waiver of the examination must submit documentation showing satisfaction of the requirements of 37 CFR § 11.7(d)(1), (d)(2), or (d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required submission items include: Application for Registration [PTO-158]; Undertaking Under 37 CFR § 11.10(b) [PTO-275] if not previously submitted; appropriate application fee; official transcripts (may be provided by OHR with notation that original is in personnel file). Place an 'X' on PTO-158 to request waiver and provide all relevant documentation with application.

rubrics_metrics.name: All business with the USPTO transacted in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: All business with the USPTO should be transacted in writing; personal attendance is unnecessary. An action of OED with regard to an application will be based exclusively on the written record in the Office (see 37 CFR § 1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must maintain written updates and correspondence; telephone, fax, or email may not substitute for required written submissions where regulation requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of aliens and limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: No grant of registration except under 37 CFR § 11.6(c). Applicants who are not U.S. citizens and do not reside in the U.S. are not eligible for registration except as permitted by § 11.6(c). Lawful permanent residents may apply for registration; other aliens residing in U.S. may apply for limited recognition under 37 CFR § 11.9(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who are aliens must provide copies of all documents submitted to and received from immigration authorities, showing authorization to reside and to work or be trained in the U.S. Documentation must show that recognition is consistent with authorized capacity of employment/training. Pending immigration approvals at time of application result in denial of admission to the examination. Qualifying aliens under 8 CFR § 274a.12(b) or (c) are not registered upon passing; they may receive limited recognition only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible applicants — convictions rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant convicted of a felony, or a crime involving moral turpitude or breach of trust, is not eligible for registration or to apply for registration during the time of any sentence (including confinement or deferred adjudication) and for two years after successful completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole (see 37 CFR § 11.7(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Conviction’ includes confession, guilty verdict/judgment, any entered plea (including nolo contendere or Alford plea), or receipt of deferred adjudication. Applicant must file required fees and the OED Director will determine satisfactory proof of reform and rehabilitation, including a sufficient period of exemplary conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible applicants — disciplined professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has been disbarred from practice or who resigned a professional license in lieu of disciplinary proceeding is ineligible to apply for registration for five years from date of disbarment or resignation. An applicant suspended on ethical grounds is ineligible until expiration of suspension (see 37 CFR § 11.7(h)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If combined with conviction, ineligibility continues until conditions of both relevant provisions are satisfied. Applicant must submit required fees for determinations by OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible applicants — previously denied for lack of present good moral character and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant refused registration for failure to demonstrate present good moral character and reputation is ineligible to reapply for two years after the date of decision (unless shorter period ordered). An applicant who withdrew during investigation is ineligible to reapply for two years after withdrawal (see 37 CFR § 11.7(k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applicants must pay fees required by 37 CFR and have burden of showing fitness to practice; must pass registration examination even if previously passed. Withdrawal during investigation is treated as obtaining a determination for fee purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing requirements and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate must apply to OED by completing a registration application form and submitting all required documentation and government fees. Applications must be complete; facsimiles will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply online at Exam Applicant Portal or mail required items to Mailstop OED. Required items: PTO-158; $118 application fee (non-refundable) or higher fee if applicable; $226 registration examination fee; official transcripts; course descriptions (Category B); other required documentation (immigration documents, responses to background questions). Strongly recommended not to file incomplete applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for completing Form PTO-158 (signature, name, ID, and updates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper application must be completed in permanent ink or computer and personally signed in accordance with 37 CFR § 1.4(e). Provide full legal name (first, middle not initial, last); name in line 1b must match government-issued photo ID. All changes to application (including address) must be reported in writing within 30 days and signed/dated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide complete legal name may result in incomplete application. OED will communicate using the complete legal name. No changes accepted by phone, fax, or email. Applicant must continue to update application until registered and keep copies of updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and admission to testing center
rubrics_metrics.description: For admission to the examination, applicant must bring a current, valid State or Federal government issued ID containing photograph and signature; name on ID must match exactly the name on line 1b of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single ID with photo and signature suffices. Admission will be denied if ID invalid/expired or name mismatch. Admission letter is not acceptable. No name changes permitted at testing centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing administration by Prometric and test delivery rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination is computer-based and administered by Prometric. Prometric provides test centers, a 15-minute tutorial before the exam, a 15-minute survey after, scratch paper and pencil (provided), continuous video monitoring, and site proctoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not bring reference materials, notes, or scratch paper into the testing area; only scratch paper provided may be used and will be collected and destroyed. Optional one-hour timed lunch break; unscheduled breaks permitted but timing continues. Cheating will result in escort from testing area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and rescheduling the examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants schedule/reschedule through Prometric website or Prometric toll-free number reserved for USPTO takers. Testing center emergencies may result in rescheduling to first available appointment at no additional charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant who does not appear for a scheduled examination will lose eligibility at Prometric and forfeits all fees previously paid to the USPTO. If insufficient testing period remains to reset eligibility, applicant must reapply to be admitted for another examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing center protocols and security procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must sign a signature log; an electronic photograph taken; entry/exit times recorded and signature verified against photo ID; continuous video monitoring; cheating (copying/photographing questions/answers, bringing notes, recording answers elsewhere, leaving and checking notes) prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prometric Test Center Administrators proctor continuously. Violation leads to removal and possible consequences. Only scratch paper and pencil provided allowed; not permitted to remove scratch paper. One optional timed hour lunch break, no other scheduled breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing failed examination questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of mailing date of notice of results, unsuccessful applicants may review (but not copy) the questions and answers they answered incorrectly by computer at a Prometric site or at OED; only one review session per exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notes may be taken and copies may not be obtained. Review session must be scheduled with Prometric or OED as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplying after failure — timing and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsuccessful applicant may reapply after receiving notice of failure but must wait 30 days after the date of the last examination before retaking. To reapply, submit PTO-158, $118 application fee (non-refundable), $226 registration examination fee, and all necessary documentation to update application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants subject to prior determinations regarding moral character must follow differing fee rules (see Bulletin). Eligibility for retesting is controlled by OED; do not contact Prometric about eligibility to retake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of USPTO fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The $118 application fee is non-refundable. The $226 registration examination fee is non-refundable after OED receives an application except in limited cases. Refunds governed by 35 U.S.C. § 42(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant submitted $1,806 under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(10) and is denied admission to the exam, the $1,806 will be refunded less $118. Applicant admitted and then withdraws, or fails to appear, must file another application and pay fees again. Fees not paid by mistake or in excess are non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of regulations regarding the examination (petition under 37 CFR § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition may be filed under 37 CFR § 11.3 requesting in writing that a requirement of the regulations (not a statutory requirement) be suspended or waived in an extraordinary situation when justice requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition is available where extraordinary circumstances justify suspension/waiver of a regulatory requirement; statute-based requirements cannot be waived by this petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful completion — moral character investigation and registration steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon successful completion or waiver of the examination, the OED Director will solicit information concerning the applicant’s moral character and reputation and may conduct an investigation if adverse information is received. Applicants passing the exam must complete registration formalities; attorneys must submit certificate of good standing (less than six months old) from highest state court to be registered as attorney; otherwise will be registered as patent agent or design patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant passing the exam who does not complete registration or limited recognition process within two years from date of notice of passing must retake and pass the exam (see 37 CFR §§ 11.8(b),(c)). The certificate of good standing should be filed with the Data Sheet (FORM PTO 107A) following receipt of notice of passing; do not file with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing under 37 CFR § 1.8
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of mailing must be deposited in the envelope with the mailed materials; each paper must have its own certificate of mailing or the certificate must identify each submitted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate must be included in the envelope and identify the correspondence. The certificate must state the date and include signature and printed name. If multiple papers submitted, each paper needs its own certificate or identification on the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Privacy Act advisory and routine uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority for collection is 35 U.S.C. §§1.6 and 31; furnishing is voluntary, principal purpose is to maintain information related to eligibility and fitness for registration. If applicant does not furnish information, they will not be admitted or registered. Information may be published or disclosed for listed routine uses (e.g., Official Gazette publication, disclosure to government agencies, courts, congressional offices, contractors, OMB, OPM, NARA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that information may be used in investigations and may be disclosed to other agencies for enforcement or personnel actions; disclosures are governed by Privacy Act routine uses.
